reason: Outcome correspondence is unresolved: the supplied description names valuing, whereas the first survey explicitly measures desires and the other study on the cited pages measures moral beliefs. No candidate was selected. Independently, both results sections print condition means and p < 0.05 for a t-test, but neither a named standardized effect size nor a numeric t statistic. Valuing findings in section 2 are secondary reports of Knobe and Roedder, not Gonnerman’s primary target test.
location: p. 198, section 3.1 (PDF p. 7); p. 199, section 3.2 (PDF p. 8); section 2, pp. 194–196
quote: Whereas Knobe and Roedder asked about Georges’ states of valuing, we asked ... about their desires. ... A t-test revealed that the difference between these means scores is ... statistically significant (p < 0.05).
